===  chart.py
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022],
    'Youth Population (15-24)': [118.2, 119.5, 120.8, 122.1, 123.4, 124.7, 126.0, 127.3],
    'Enrolled in Secondary Education': [82.3, 83.1, 83.9, 84.7, 85.5, 86.3, 87.1, 87.9],
    'Completed Secondary Education': [68.9, 69.5, 70.1, 70.8, 71.2, 71.5, 71.9, 72.3],
    'Entered Labor Force': [62.8, 63.5, 64.2, 64.8, 65.3, 65.7, 66.1, 66.5],
    'Secured Formal Employment': [40.7, 41.2, 41.6, 42.0, 42.5, 42.8, 43.1, 43.4],
    'Unemployed (6+ months)': [23.1, 22.9, 22.7, 22.6, 22.5, 22.8, 23.0, 23.3],
    'Underemployed (Part-time/Informal)': [19.3, 19.1, 18.9, 18.8, 18.7, 18.9, 19.2, 19.5],
    'In Informal Sector (No Benefits)': [15.4, 15.1, 14.8, 14.5, 14.2, 14.4, 14.7, 15.0],
    'Long-term Unemployed (12+ months)': [9.0, 8.8, 8.6, 8.5, 8.3, 8.7, 9.0, 9.3]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df.set_index('Year', inplace=True)

fig = go.Figure()

colors = [
    '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728',
    '#9467bd', '#8c564b', '#e377c2', '#7f7f7f', '#bcbd22'
]

stages = [
    'Youth Population (15-24)',
    'Enrolled in Secondary Education',
    'Completed Secondary Education',
    'Entered Labor Force',
    'Secured Formal Employment',
    'Unemployed (6+ months)',
    'Underemployed (Part-time/Informal)',
    'In Informal Sector (No Benefits)',
    'Long-term Unemployed (12+ months)'
]

for i, stage in enumerate(stages):
    if stage != 'In Informal Sector (No Benefits)':
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=df.index,
            y=df[stage],
            mode='lines',
            stackgroup='one',
            name=stage,
            line=dict(width=0.5, color=colors[i]),
            fillcolor=colors[i]
        ))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Trends in Youth Employment Pathways: Sub-Saharan Africa (2015-2022)',
    xaxis_title='Year',
    yaxis_title='Number of Youth (Millions)',
    showlegend=True,
    legend_title='Employment Stage',
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        yanchor="bottom",
        y=1.02,
        xanchor="right",
        x=1
    ),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, t=80, b=50),
    hovermode='x unified',
    plot_bgcolor='white'
)

fig.write_image('output.png', scale=2)
===  summary.txt
This image is a stacked area chart illustrating the trends in youth employment pathways in Sub-Saharan Africa from 2015 to 2022. The chart visualizes the distribution of the youth population (ages 15-24) across various stages of education and employment, with each category represented by a distinct color.

The x-axis represents the years from 2015 to 2022, while the y-axis denotes the number of youth in millions. The chart includes several overlapping layers, each corresponding to a specific employment or educational stage. At the base, the deep blue area represents the total youth population, steadily increasing from around 118.2 million in 2015 to approximately 127.3 million in 2022.

Above this, the orange segment shows youths enrolled in secondary education, starting at about 82.3 million in 2015 and rising to around 87.9 million by 2022. The next layer, in green, indicates those who have completed secondary education, growing from roughly 68.9 million in 2015 to 72.3 million in 2022.

The red area represents youths who have entered the labor force, increasing modestly from approximately 62.8 million in 2015 to 66.5 million in 2022. Above this, the purple section shows those who secured formal employment, rising from 40.7 million to 43.4 million over the same period.

The brown segment depicts youths unemployed for six or more months, remaining relatively stable around 23 million. Overlapping this, the pink area represents underemployed youths working part-time or in informal roles, slightly fluctuating around 19 million. The grey segment above it indicates those in the informal sector without benefits, showing a minor decrease from 15.4 million in 2015 to 15.0 million in 2022.

Finally, the thin yellow top layer represents long-term unemployed youths (12+ months), starting at 9.0 million in 2015, dipping slightly, and then rising back to around 9.3 million by 2022. The stacked nature of the chart effectively displays how the youth population is distributed across these different stages over the years.

args.message:
**Data fix:** chart.py skipped the 'In Informal Sector (No Benefits)' series in its plotting loop. summary.txt describes this series as the grey layer, falling from 15.4 to 15.0 million. I removed the exclusion, so all 9 stages are now plotted.

**Checked on the figure object:**
- It has 9 traces.
- Each trace's values match table.csv exactly.
- The informal-sector trace is grey (#7f7f7f), as the summary says.
- The title text is unchanged.

**Readability fix:** adding the ninth entry made the horizontal legend wrap to 5 rows, and it collided with the title. I made two layout changes only:
- raised the top margin from 80 to 200;
- pinned the title near the top of the figure (`title_y=0.97`, `title_yanchor='top'`).

In the rendered output.png the title, legend and plot no longer overlap. Colours, labels, the axes and the legend's position and orientation are unchanged.
